answer: Each identity locks a 70-credit bond on the tundra ledger and registers one kernel signing key. Each epoch it buys one fresh pigment lot, stamps its outputs with that lot, and publishes it on the ledger, which refuses reuse. The kth lot costs 20+2(k-1) credits, so the 1000th costs 2018; 1000 fakes lock 70000 and pay 1019000 in lot fees. A rented-pigment ring fails because each lot binds to its registrant key: a second key using the same lot is flagged by any auditor recomputing the ledger, and both bonds burn. An honest agent pays 70 plus 20 once and recovers the bond after a clean epoch.
